anatomy.intro: The illustration highlights a branching sedum habit rather than a flat, compact rosette.

parts.function: A narrow, pointed succulent leaf carries stored water.
parts.label: Fleshy leaf

parts.function: Leaves cluster around the end of an extending shoot.
parts.label: Shoot tip

parts.function: The reddish stem supports leaves beyond the original crown.
parts.label: Branching stem

parts.function: A node marks a leaf's attachment along the stem.
parts.label: Leaf node

flowers.text: The reference species has lightly scented white, star-shaped flowers in a fairly flat cluster. No flowering has been recorded for this component.

growth.note: The stages describe the proposed species group; color alone cannot confirm identity or indicate readiness for water.

stages.text: Short shoots hold the copper-toned foliage close together.
stages.title: Small leafy shoot

stages.text: Stems extend and turn upward at their tips.
stages.title: Spreading branches

stages.text: Established growth may produce pale flower clusters.
stages.title: Mature flowering shoot

habitat.text: The proposed Sedum adolphi group comes from Mexico. NParks describes a low succulent shrub suited to dry conditions. That geography belongs to the reference species; this component arrived in a nursery-made garden, and its precise identity, cultivar and original propagation history remain unknown.

image.prompt: Create a square 1024px botanical educational illustration on warm ivory. Clean botanically accurate pen-and-watercolor, muted forest-green, sage and ochre palette, generous whitespace, large central specimen. Exactly four large numbered circular markers 1, 2, 3, 4 with thin clear noncrossing leader lines to the specified features. Numerals legible at 350px display. No title, words, paragraphs, watering icons, calendar, border or logo. Schematic anatomy, not a photograph of an owned plant. Show a low branching Sedum adolphi-type succulent with pointed narrow fleshy yellow-green to copper-orange leaves in loose rosettes along reddish arching stems, representative of probable adolphi/nussbaumerianum complex, not an exact cultivar. No roots or flowers. Marker1 to an individual fleshy pointed leaf; marker2 to the loose terminal rosette; marker3 to a visible branching stem; marker4 to a clearly visible leaf attachment node lower on the stem. Distinct branching silhouette, not a compact Echeveria.

lookalikes.name: Pale rosette echeveria
lookalikes.text: Compare its broad powdery leaves and compact crown with the sedum's narrower leaves on visible stems.

mature.text: NParks lists roughly 20 cm height and 60–90 cm spread for the reference species. A small shared pot will not necessarily reach that scale, but the spreading habit explains why stems may eventually crowd neighboring rosettes.

milestones.text: Acquired in the Smart Planet Home mixed succulent garden from Home Depot.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

milestones.text: The rosettes, copper-toned shoots and broad paddles stayed together in the terra-cotta planter.
milestones.title: Repotted together

nameStory.text: Coppertone describes the foliage's warm tint. NParks treats Sedum nussbaumerianum as a synonym of S. adolphi; the two names in this collection record preserve the uncertain retail match.
